guides.title: Halal, explained
guides.summary: What permissible food means, how sourcing and preparation matter, and why ingredient lists are only part of the picture.

sections.heading: Start with the meaning
sections.text: Halal is an Arabic term meaning permissible. For food, suitability involves ingredients as well as relevant preparation and handling practices.

sections.heading: Labels need context
sections.text: A halal logo on a mockup is not independent proof of certification. For meat and prepared foods, ask who certified the product, for which site and scope, and whether the certification remains valid.

sections.heading: A welcoming beginning
sections.text: Halal foods can be enjoyed by anyone. Muslim dietary requirements may differ across interpretations; consult qualified sources for religious rulings.

guides.title: What makes something tayyib?
guides.summary: Explore why goodness, quality, clarity, and responsible choices matter alongside what is permissible.

sections.heading: Beyond a label
sections.text: Tayyib is commonly associated with goodness and wholesomeness. It encourages us to ask how food is prepared, presented, sourced and shared.

sections.heading: Everyday practice
sections.text: Look for clear ingredients, safe food handling, reasonable portions, and respect for different households and traditions.

guides.title: Reading ingredients with confidence
guides.summary: A practical guide to questions worth asking about ingredients, flavourings, processing and certification.

sections.heading: Questions to ask
sections.text: Check animal-derived ingredients, processing aids, gelatine, flavouring carriers and any alcohol-related ingredients. If details are unclear, ask the manufacturer or certifier.

sections.heading: Evidence over assumptions
sections.text: A product is not necessarily halal merely because it is vegetarian-looking or free of pork. Halal assurance depends on its actual ingredients, processing and any relevant certification.

sections.heading: Check the date and scope
sections.text: Certification can be time-limited and may apply only to named products or facilities. Verify the relevant version and authority.

guides.title: Finding your community in Jamaica
guides.summary: Find public mosque directories, ask about visits, and discover where local organizations publish community information.

sections.heading: Begin with published local sources
sections.text: The Jamaica Foundation for Islamic Charity publishes mosque and business directories. Contact a mosque directly to confirm prayer times, facilities and visitor arrangements.

sections.heading: Respect every visitor
sections.text: People approach religious communities with different backgrounds and expectations. Ask about local practices rather than assuming.

recipes.title: Island-style beef curry
recipes.summary: Slow-simmered beef, fragrant curry, potatoes and fresh thyme — made for sharing.
steps: Season beef and allow the flavour to develop.
Cook onion, garlic and curry powder gently before adding beef.
Add liquid, cover and simmer until beef is tender and safely cooked.
Add potatoes and carrot; simmer until soft. Serve with rice or steamed vegetables.

recipes.title: Jerk beef skewers
recipes.summary: Smoky beef, sweet peppers and red onion with lively island seasoning.
steps: Mix the beef with seasoning and oil.
Thread meat and cut vegetables onto skewers.
Grill or bake, turning regularly, until safely cooked throughout.
Serve with rice and peas or a crisp salad.

recipes.title: Golden seasoned vegetables
recipes.summary: A colourful tray of roasted vegetables with a generous seasoning finish.
steps: Roast, turning once, until golden and tender.
